summary: Jeffrey Stout is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Brown University, Princeton University (PhD), and the California Culinary Academy. He served as a professor at Princeton University from 1976 to 2018.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Jeffrey Wayne Bass studied at the University of North Carolina Wilmington, the University of Tennessee, and UCLA (PhD) under Gregory Schopen. He has held teaching posts at UCLA and UC San Diego.

Jenkuan Shih is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2006) supervised by Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi.

Jens Braarvig is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He held professorships at the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology around 2002 and at the University of Oslo in 2003.
Jens Peter Laut specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Klaus Röhrborn in 2008 and held a post at the University of Göttingen around 2008.

Jens Schlieter works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, studying at the University of Vienna and the University of Bonn (PhD under Josef Simon). He became Professor for Theory of Religion at the University of Bern around 2005.

Jens-Uwe Hartmann is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology educated at the University of Munich and the University of Göttingen. He held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin (1995–1999) and the University of Munich (1999–2018).
Jeong-Eun Kim, a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, completed a PhD at SOAS University of London by 2011 under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

Jerome Silbergeld, a sinologist and art historian, earned degrees from Stanford University and the University of Oregon. He served as Chair of Art History at the University of Washington (~1975–2001) and professor at Princeton University (~2001–2018).

Jerzy Bańczerowski studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961). Working in linguistics, he served there as head of the Department of General and Comparative Linguistics (1969) and as professor (1977–1991).

Jerzy Kuryłowicz was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Lviv (~1920–1923) and under Antoine Meillet (~1921–1923). He held academic posts at the University of Lviv (~1926–1946) and Jagiellonian University (~1946–1965).

Jessie Pons is a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed a doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University in 2011. As of 2019, she was Junior Professor at Ruhr University Bochum.
Jian Ouyang worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Yang Renshan (~1904–1911). He founded and served as head of the China Institute of Inner Learning from around 1922 to 1943.

Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Nankai University and completed his doctorate at Harvard University (attested 2002) before serving as a professor at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).
Jianming Hu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a researcher post at Komazawa University (attested 2015).

Jiayao An, a specialist in history, archaeology, and sinology, studied under Su Bai (~1978–1982). She has held posts at the Institute of Archaeology, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1982) and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Jien Abe was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who undertook graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). He served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.

Jigdal Dagchen Sakya was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar who studied under Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse. He held a post at the University of Washington from around 1960 to 1963.

Jigme Chhoeda is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Druk Sangag Choeling and Tango monasteries. He served as Abbot of Tango Monastery (~1986) and held leadership roles with the Central Monastic Body and Dratshang Lhentshog.
Jigme Tenpai Nyima was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
